blocks.text: Luke watched Seth’s hand.
Seth kept his fingers over the bent edge. He stopped pressing, though every part of him wanted to pull.
“What are you doing?” Luke asked.
“Trying to get comfortable.”
Luke glanced at the steel around Seth’s boots. “Good luck.”
From the yard, Billy’s voice came through the front room. “What demonstration needs a locked chair?”
“You’ll never get away with this,” Seth said.
Daniel glanced back through the open workshop doorway. “You’re hardly in a position to stop me.”
Jenny lifted her head. “Kidnapping. Gas. A reporter fastened to a chair. You’ve practically written my next article.”
“You won’t be writing anything.”
“Then stop giving me material.”
Luke stayed beside the chairs, watching them. Daniel turned back to Billy and pulled the service door wide open.
“Go home, Billy.” He stepped into the threshold, close enough that Billy could have caught his sleeve. “This has nothing to do with you.”
Billy stayed on the flat yard landing. “Then why can I hear my missing reporter from here?”

As Billy pressed for an answer, Luke drifted toward the inner doorway, turning his back on the chairs to listen. He stopped just inside it, where the rolled-aside shelving blocked his view of Jenny’s feet and the cage corner. Daniel remained in the service threshold, facing Billy.
Jenny waited until Luke’s eyes were on his uncle.
Then her shoes began to move.
Small movements, quick and even. Her head felt clearer than it had, but she kept her breathing slow. Beneath the chair, a point of light gathered between her toes.
She tipped one shoe outward. A short tap sent the little ball against the projecting fastening on the outside of her left ankle cuff.
blocks.alt: Jenny, in a white blouse and pink skirt, keeps both wrists cuffed while a small plasma ball heats an ankle cuff beside her ordinary shoe. Restrained Seth sits nearby.

blocks.text: The metal brightened. Heat reached her stocking, and she stopped moving at once. The light died.
Jenny waited for the hot prickle to ease. Her shoe was an ordinary shoe. She could smell its warming leather.
She tried again with a smaller ball, touching the same outer fastening in brief taps and letting each glow fade before making another. She kept her toes below the hot metal and her skirt clear of it.
At last the softened fastening parted. The cuff fell open against the chair leg.

She drew her ankle away without touching its bright edge. With that foot free, she had room to work at the other fastening. Another small ball, another short kick. She paused when the heat crept inward, then finished the cut.
Both feet reached the floor. Her wrists still held her to the armrests.
Across the room, Fist lifted one eye toward her.
Jenny looked from him to the upper corner of his cage. No bottles stood between her chair and that corner. Fist lay low on the opposite side, his torn white cuff crumpled beneath him.
She shifted in the chair as far as her pinned wrists allowed. This time she could move her feet properly. A small ball gathered low between her shoes.
Luke leaned toward the doorway. “Uncle Daniel?”
Jenny planted one foot and kicked with the other.
The plasma struck high on the cage, well above Fist’s damaged leather. A short section of bars glowed, softened and sagged apart. The light faded against the bare metal tray beneath the cage.
blocks.alt: With her wrists still cuffed and her legs free, Jenny kicks plasma into an upper corner of the single cage, above the injured red glove resting at its bottom.

blocks.text: Fist stared at the opening. Then he pushed himself up.

He listed sideways. His cuff scraped the cage floor, and he shut his eyes for a moment before trying again. This time he reached the gap. He squeezed through below the hot ends, drawing his torn cuff carefully after him.
A loose bar dropped onto the tray with a sharp clink.
Luke turned.
Fist came at him from the side, low and crooked. Luke had just enough time to see red leather.
The punch struck the side of his iron jaw and knocked him away from the doorway.
blocks.alt: Battered Fist strikes the side of Luke’s iron jaw as the floating blond head turns. One cage with a melted upper opening is behind them; the high basement window has a glass pane swung open.

blocks.text: Fist swerved past him. The effort pulled at his creased side, and his next rise barely cleared the bench. Above it, the high window still stood open from when Daniel had admitted Luke with his prisoner. Its pane was swung clear.
Fist squeezed through into the sunken yard. He crossed toward the opposite wall, then struggled upward past the railing.
Luke shook himself and shot after him.
Outside, Flaming Head rose from beside the window. Fist passed above him, flying toward the roofs with Luke close behind.
At the first chimney, Fist tried a sharp turn. His damaged cuff dragged, and he dropped below the roof edge. Luke cut across the corner and gained on him.
Fist hauled himself up again. Iron teeth were almost level with his cuff.
Flaming Head rose straight into Luke’s path.
Luke swerved. Flaming Head moved with him, leaving Fist room to turn behind. Fist saw the gap and took it, though he came around lower than he meant to.
Luke checked over his shoulder. The glove was behind him now; the fiery face waited ahead.
blocks.alt: Above Cleveland’s rooftops, Luke’s floating blond head faces Flaming Head ahead while scuffed Fist, with a torn white cuff, approaches from behind at a lower height. A recessed stair area is visible below.

blocks.text: He darted toward the open space above a roof. Flaming Head rose to meet him. Fist edged across the lower route, unable to climb as quickly. Luke feinted toward the glove, then snapped back toward Flaming Head, who slipped aside before the teeth reached him.
Neither Luke nor Fist heard words from the fire. Fist watched where Flaming Head moved and tried to keep the other side covered.
Inside, Seth heard the iron jaws click past the window and away.
He pressed against the bent cuff again. His head no longer tipped with every breath. The steel gave beneath his thumb, slowly flattening until he could draw his right hand clear.

He gripped the cuff around his left wrist and peeled it away from the armrest. Then he leaned down. One ankle cuff tore loose at its mounting. He bent it open and removed it from his boot before bending the other cuff open beneath both hands.
For a moment he sat with all four restraints hanging clear, hardly believing there was nothing left to stop him.
Jenny tugged at her wrists. He was beside her before she could ask.
“Hold still.”
He braced the first cuff away from her skin and bent the steel outward. She slipped her hand free. He did the same to the second.
Jenny caught his sleeve as she stood. He caught her elbow. Neither quite let go.
“You’re up,” he said.
“So are you.” She glanced toward the window. “Fist needs us.”
They started around the bench, leaving the cooling ankle cuffs behind.
At the service entrance, Daniel stopped answering Billy.
He had heard the clink, the blow and the rush past the window. Now something heavier scraped inside. He turned toward the workshop.
“Luke?”
Billy stepped nearer the open threshold. Through the front room and the inner doorway, he saw a red glove on a boy’s hand reach past the bench. Jenny appeared beside him.
Daniel saw them too. Still standing in the threshold, he turned to go back inside.
“Stay out of this, Billy.”
Billy knew where Daniel was going. Jenny had only just reached the doorway. Daniel would reach her first.
Billy was still outside, scarcely an arm’s length away. Before Daniel could step back through the doorway, Billy raised his hand.
Billy was not used to hitting people. He had one good punch in him.
He landed it.
blocks.alt: Billy stands on the sunken yard landing and lands one punch within ordinary arm’s reach of Daniel at the wide-open basement service doorway. Brick retaining walls and the yard steps surround them.

blocks.text: Daniel’s knees folded. He dropped across the open doorway, his shoulders on the yard landing, and did not move.
Billy crouched immediately, his punching hand tucked against his chest. He watched Daniel’s coat rise with a breath, then another.
“Help!” he called up the steps. “We need an ambulance down here!”
Seth and Jenny came through the front room. Jenny knelt beside Billy while Seth held the service door wide.
“He’s breathing,” Billy said. His voice sounded thinner than before. “He hasn’t woken.”
Over the yard, Luke plunged beneath Fist’s uneven approach. Flaming Head turned after him, blocking the way back toward the window.
Luke descended over the open sunken yard, below the railing. From there he could see the service landing.
His uncle lay across the same open service doorway, his head and shoulders in plain view on the landing. Billy and Jenny crouched next to him.
“Uncle Daniel!”
Luke dropped straight toward them.
“Back!” Seth called.
He pulled Jenny clear. Billy scrambled against the doorframe as Luke swept down. The iron jaws closed around a fold at the back of Daniel’s lab coat, clear of his neck and shoulders.
The coat pulled tight. Daniel lifted from the landing, limp and silent.
Seth stepped forward, then stopped short of the iron teeth. Luke was already rising through the yard with his uncle hanging beneath him, just as he had carried him away after the robot fell.
He did not look back at the workshop or the people below.
Fist turned to follow. He managed a few yards above the railing before his damaged side buckled and he lost height.
Flaming Head dropped beside him. Fist tried to climb again, failed, and sank toward the yard steps.
“Leave them!” Jenny called. “Come down to us!”
Seth reached the steps in time to hold out both hands. Fist settled across his gloves with a small, pained grunt.
“Easy,” Seth said. “I’ve got you.”
Above the roofs, Luke disappeared with Daniel. Fist lifted his eyes after them, but made no second attempt.

Billy looked back through the open entrance. The collector stood empty beyond the bench, its loose wire hanging where Daniel had left it. Papers covered the work surface. The broken cage and restraints were still there.
“We’ll tell the police exactly where it is,” he said. “First, up the steps.”
He helped Jenny to the railing. Seth carried Fist, keeping the torn cuff from catching against the brickwork. Flaming Head rose beside them, still outside.
At the top, a woman from the neighboring shop hurried into the alley.
“I heard you. I’ve called for an ambulance.”
“Thank you,” Billy said. “Tell them one injured friend is here, two people have been gassed, and an unconscious man has been carried away. I’ll explain.”
He gave her the laboratory address and asked her to pass it to the police as well. Then he stood with the others on the street, clear of the yard entrance.
Jenny breathed in. There was bus exhaust in the air, and warm pavement, and somebody’s lunch from the shop. She could move both arms. She could walk away from that door.

Billy folded the loose bottom of his trench coat over his good forearm. Seth lowered Fist onto it, carefully supporting the glove until Billy had him settled. Flaming Head hovered nearby, watching the alley and the roofs.
Jenny noticed Billy holding his other hand stiffly.
“Are you all right?”
“Ask me tomorrow.”
Fist opened one eye. “Ask me then too.”
Billy adjusted the folded cloth beneath him. “You’re first.”

They began moving toward the shop entrance, where there was a chair and room to wait for help. Billy went a few paces ahead with Fist resting safely on his arm. Flaming Head kept close above the awning.
Jenny caught Seth’s hand.
“Thank you for coming for me.”
He looked back toward the alley. “I didn’t exactly get the rescue part right.”
“You’re here. We both are.”
“You got your own feet free,” he said. “And Fist. I couldn’t have got you out without that.”
“Then we helped each other.”
She leaned over and kissed his cheek.
blocks.alt: Two panels show Jenny kissing masked Seth on the cheek, then crouching beside him as he sits on the sidewalk with a yellow banana peel on his hair, next to a tipped garbage can and its lid. Billy holds injured Fist safely nearby.

blocks.text: Seth stopped walking. Color rose beneath his red mask and spread all the way to his ears.
“I—yes. I mean—”

He tried to take another step while still looking at her. His boot caught the garbage can beside the shop wall. The can tipped, its lid clattered away, and Seth landed on his bottom on the sidewalk. A few paper scraps spilled after him. A banana peel flopped onto his hair.
Jenny crouched beside him. “Are you hurt?”
Seth tested his elbows, then looked up at her. “No. I think I sat down.”
She lifted the peel from his head. He stared at it, then let out a small laugh. Jenny smiled and offered her hand.
From Billy’s coat, Fist’s eye opened again.
“I’m all right,” Seth assured him, taking Jenny’s hand.
Back on his feet, he set the can upright and gathered the paper scraps. Jenny dropped the peel inside while he fetched the lid.
When he had fitted it back, she slipped her hand into his again.
Ahead, Billy held the shop door for them with his shoulder, Fist snug against his coat, while Flaming Head waited above the awning.
Seth and Jenny walked toward them together. Seth was still blushing.
